frozenBefore: any pilot training run was started

strategy.description: Fine-tune the v1 checkpoint on a mixture of GuitarSet solo-guitar batches (rehearsal) and Slakh full-band batches (new domain), keeping the v1 objective and the four exported heads unchanged.
rationale: Measured: the rule engine reaches 0.519 detailed accuracy on full-band audio while v1 reaches 0.255 and full-v2 0.278. The learned models do not transfer from solo guitar to dense mixtures, and that transfer gap - not decoding - is the bottleneck worth attacking.

Measured: perfect harmonic separation buys only +0.007 to +0.043 detailed accuracy, and isolating the guitar stem COSTS every engine (-0.03 to -0.17). Effort therefore belongs in the chord model, not in separation or in a guitar-isolating front end.

Measured: full-v2's no-chord head is inert on full-band audio (P/R/F1 all near 0.01 on every view) while v1 retains 0.34-0.42 F1. Starting from v1 rather than full-v2 keeps a working no-chord head, which the full-band gates require.
Rehearsal is required because GuitarSet preservation is a hard gate: a full-band model that forgets solo guitar is not an improvement to the actual product use case.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Oracle separation gains are within +0.04 detailed accuracy; the oracle-guitar view is actively worse than the full mix. Improving separation cannot close a 0.26 gap.
full-v2's no-chord head does not survive the domain shift (F1 ~0.01). Starting there would inherit a broken head that the full-band no-chord gate depends on.
Defensible, but it adds a schedule hyperparameter that CPU-only budget cannot afford to validate, and the oracle-vs-mix gap it exploits is measured to be small.
Guarantees GuitarSet regression beyond the frozen preservation gates and cannot be recovered within one CPU pilot.

domainSampling.note: Frozen before any pilot result. An even split is the least-assumption choice that keeps the preservation gate reachable while giving the new domain equal weight.
domainSampling.slakhViewNote: Guitar-only views are excluded deliberately: they measured WORSE than the full mix for every engine, so training on them would optimise for a view that carries less harmonic context.

candidates.note: Reduced learning rate because this is a fine-tune from a converged checkpoint, not a fresh run.
Same schedule, GuitarSet batches only. Separates the effect of continued training from the effect of adding the full-band domain.

cpuBudget.note: Must not start while the boundary-calibration study is still training.

evaluation.fullBandDevelopment: Slakh validation split only; the untouched test split is never used for selection.
evaluation.guitarSetPreservation: p01-p05 leave-one-performer-out development metrics, both captures; p00 stays sealed.

knownLimitations: Reference labels are note-level (~0.6 s mean region, ~100 regions/minute vs ~20 for GuitarSet human annotations). Accuracy and no-chord metrics are meaningful; the frozen full-band fragmentation gate cannot honestly be applied to them and will be reported as not-evaluable rather than passed.
The percussion-only control is scored against harmonic labels rather than an all-no-chord reference, so the frozen noChordRecallMinimum gate cannot be evaluated as written.
Slakh renders a guitar in 1707 of 1709 usable tracks, so guitar-absent behaviour can only be read from the guitar-absent-harmonic view, not from a natural subset.
Slakh2100 is rendered from MIDI. Even a fully passing pilot is synthetic-domain evidence and does not establish production readiness.
